answer: A nullifier registry stops one secret spawning many identities. Each applicant publishes one nullifier from a secret and locks 55 credits to the garden plot it claims. A repeat registration repeats the tag, so raven auditors link the pair and burn both deposits. Rewards flow only to identities with a crystal record, leaving the pair unpaid. The named failure is nullifier rental: a rented secret leaves the same tag, so renter and owner fall together. The kth fake costs a fresh secret and 55 credits, so 1,000 fakes need 55,000 credits, while one honest agent pays 55 once.
